pharm: A dihydropyridine calcium-channel antagonist that blocks the L-type calcium channels of vascular smooth muscle, producing peripheral arterial vasodilatation, reduced systemic vascular resistance and lowered blood pressure with minimal direct effect on cardiac contractility or conduction.

summary: Nitrendipine is a dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker used for the treatment of hypertension. It acts mainly on peripheral arterial smooth muscle to lower systemic vascular resistance and blood pressure, with little direct effect on the heart. It is notable as the active treatment in the landmark Syst-Eur trial, which demonstrated reduced stroke and cardiovascular events when treating isolated systolic hypertension in elderly patients. The usual dose is 10 mg once daily, increased to 20 mg daily (once or twice daily) according to response. The common adverse effects are the dihydropyridine class effects of peripheral (ankle) oedema, flushing, headache and palpitations. Nitrendipine is extensively metabolised in the liver (CYP3A4) with a high first-pass effect, so exposure and the blood-pressure-lowering effect are increased in hepatic impairment and a reduced dose with cautious titration is advised; grapefruit juice markedly raises its plasma levels.
indications: Treatment of hypertension (including isolated systolic hypertension in the elderly), alone or with other antihypertensives

dosage.d: 10 mg once daily in the morning
dosage.n: Take with or after food; swallow whole

dosage.d: Increase to 20 mg once daily, or 10 mg twice daily, up to 20 mg twice daily if required
dosage.n: Titrate according to blood-pressure response over weeks

dosage.d: Start at the lower 10 mg dose and titrate cautiously
dosage.n: Basis of the Syst-Eur regimen; monitor for hypotension and oedema

dosage.d: Use a reduced starting dose with careful titration
dosage.n: Increased exposure; blood-pressure-lowering effect may be enhanced

admin: Swallow tablets whole with water; take with or after food, preferably in the morning
Do not take with grapefruit juice, which greatly increases drug levels
Effect develops over hours to days; allow weeks for full blood-pressure response before increasing the dose
Do not stop abruptly without advice; rebound increases in blood pressure can occur
Continue lifestyle measures (salt restriction, weight, exercise) alongside treatment
moa: Nitrendipine is a dihydropyridine calcium-channel antagonist that selectively inhibits the influx of calcium through voltage-gated L-type channels in vascular smooth muscle. By reducing intracellular calcium it relaxes arteriolar smooth muscle, dilating peripheral resistance vessels and lowering systemic vascular resistance and arterial blood pressure. It is highly vascular-selective with little negative inotropic, chronotropic or dromotropic effect at therapeutic doses, so it does not significantly impair cardiac contractility or AV conduction. The reduction in afterload may be accompanied by a modest reflex increase in heart rate. Nitrendipine has a high first-pass hepatic metabolism, giving a relatively low and variable oral bioavailability.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to nitrendipine or other dihydropyridines
Unstable angina and within the first 4 weeks after myocardial infarction
relative: Concomitant strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or grapefruit juice
monitor: Anginal symptoms, especially early in treatment or after dose increase

preg: There are inadequate data on nitrendipine in pregnancy, and dihydropyridines have shown reproductive toxicity in animals and may relax uterine muscle. Nitrendipine is not recommended in pregnancy and should be used only if clearly necessary when no safer alternative is available; if used near term, monitor the neonate.
lact: Nitrendipine is excreted into breast milk. Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment; if therapy is essential, breastfeeding should be avoided.
renal: Nitrendipine is eliminated mainly by hepatic metabolism and is not significantly cleared unchanged by the kidneys, so no specific dose adjustment is generally required in renal impairment. Routine blood-pressure monitoring is advised as for any antihypertensive.
hepatic: Nitrendipine undergoes extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism (mainly CYP3A4). In hepatic impairment its bioavailability and plasma levels rise and the blood-pressure-lowering effect is enhanced; use a reduced starting dose with cautious titration and close monitoring, and avoid in severe impairment unless clearly justified.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir) - markedly increase nitrendipine levels and hypotensive effect
Other antihypertensives and vasodilators - additive blood-pressure lowering
moderate: CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital) - reduce nitrendipine efficacy
Beta-blockers - usually additive antihypertensive effect; monitor
Digoxin - nitrendipine may increase digoxin levels; monitor
NSAIDs / corticosteroids - may reduce antihypertensive efficacy
minor: Drugs that prolong the QT interval - theoretical additive caution
interactions.food: Grapefruit juice strongly inhibits CYP3A4 and substantially increases nitrendipine plasma levels and hypotensive effect - avoid grapefruit juice; take with or after food.
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol may potentiate the vasodilator and hypotensive effect; advise moderation.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory interference; monitor blood pressure and, if on digoxin, digoxin levels.

serious: Aggravation or precipitation of angina pectoris
emergency: Acute worsening of chest pain (myocardial ischaemia)

monitoring: Anginal symptoms, particularly at initiation and dose increases
Liver function and digoxin levels where relevant
counsel: Take the tablet once a day (or as prescribed), with or after food, at about the same time each day
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, which can raise the level of this medicine
Swelling of the ankles, flushing, headache or a fast heartbeat can occur early and often settle
Stand up slowly to avoid dizziness, especially when you start the medicine
It can take a few weeks to reach full effect on your blood pressure
Do not stop the medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor
pk: Blood-pressure effect within 1-2 hours, developing fully over days to weeks
Plasma Tmax about 1-3 hours after oral dosing
Antihypertensive effect supports once- to twice-daily dosing
Store below 25-30 C, protect from light; keep in original packaging
pearls: NOT FDA-approved; this record is derived faithfully from EMA/SmPC and BNF sources, not from openFDA
Active drug in the landmark Syst-Eur trial - reduced stroke and cardiovascular events in elderly isolated systolic hypertension
Ankle oedema, flushing and headache are dose-related dihydropyridine class effects
High first-pass CYP3A4 metabolism - avoid grapefruit juice and watch CYP3A4 inhibitor/inducer interactions
Reduce the dose and titrate cautiously in hepatic impairment (enhanced effect)
May modestly increase digoxin levels - monitor when co-prescribed
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next one at the usual time. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one.
overdose: Overdose causes excessive peripheral vasodilatation with pronounced and prolonged hypotension, often with reflex tachycardia; bradycardia and conduction effects are less typical of dihydropyridines. There is no specific antidote. Management is supportive: place the patient supine with legs elevated, give intravenous fluids, and monitor cardiovascular status. Intravenous calcium and vasopressor/inotropic support may be needed for severe hypotension; activated charcoal may be considered after recent substantial ingestion. Dialysis is not useful because nitrendipine is highly protein-bound.
